title: 1970 AHSME Problem 15
statement: Lines in the \(xy\)-plane are drawn through the point \((3,4)\) and the trisection points of the line segment joining the points \((-4,5)\) and \((5,-1).\) One of these lines has the equation:

solutions.text:
The displacement from \((-4,5)\) to \((5,-1)\) is \((9,-6).\) The trisection points are therefore \[ (-4,5)+\tfrac13(9,-6)=(-1,3) \] and \((2,1).\) The line through \((-1,3)\) and \((3,4)\) has slope \(\frac{1}{4},\) so \[ y-4=\frac14(x-3), \] or \(x-4y+13=0.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Find the two trisection points by moving one-third and two-thirds of the displacement vector
The trisection points are \((-1,3)\) and \((2,1)\); find the line from either one to \((3,4)\)
